myths.title: Name and Meaning
myths.text: The name means "Swift impetuous male deity; the Shinto storm god" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Susanō appears within the Japanese tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Susanō continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Japanese tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Susanō embodies storms, sea, chaos in the Japanese imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Susanō is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Japanese tradition.
